name: Improve the solution
description: Choose the next intervention according to the strongest observable limitation, then revisit the tree after evaluating it.
decision: what can I change to improve my solution?

children.name: Improve comparison reliability
children.description: Choose an evidence-gathering change when current scores cannot reliably distinguish candidate solutions.
children.decision: What prevents the current evaluation from supporting the next model choice?

children.name: Change the evaluation sample
children.description: Choose how to obtain a representative held-out comparison without training on its labels.
children.decision: Which evaluation design should replace the current unreliable comparison?

children.name: Score candidates locally
children.description: Evaluate candidate changes on saved held-out or out-of-fold predictions before selecting a small number for external evaluation.

children.name: Balance target distributions across folds
children.description: Create stratified folds using class labels or binned continuous targets and compare fold distributions.

children.name: Keep related observations together
children.description: Split by entity or subject, comparing grouped and stratified-grouped folds when label balancing conflicts with natural groups.

children.name: Generate aligned out-of-fold predictions
children.description: Train on shared fold indices and save predictions only for each model’s held-out rows to support honest stacking and comparison.

children.name: Check local-to-external score agreement
children.description: Compare local and external scores for a small fixed panel of existing configurations before trusting their ranking.

children.name: Change the model-selection signal
children.description: Choose whether the stopping metric, its implementation, or its computational cost is the evaluation bottleneck.
children.decision: What should change in the metric used to select training iterations?

children.name: Use the task metric for stopping
children.description: Implement the task metric as an evaluation callback and select iterations by held-out task performance.

children.name: Use a smoother stopping proxy
children.description: Compare a standard smooth evaluation metric with the custom metric for early stopping while retaining the task metric for final validation.

children.name: Repair the metric callback
children.description: Check the callback signature, label/prediction shapes, return format, and direction against small hand-verifiable examples.

children.name: Accelerate repeated metric calculation
children.description: Replace the slow metric implementation with an optimized equivalent and verify agreement on ordinary and tied predictions.

children.name: Change the experiment design
children.description: Choose the experiment that resolves the present attribution or search uncertainty.
children.decision: What experiment should be run next given the evidence already available?

children.name: Establish an end-to-end baseline
children.description: Run the simplest complete pipeline through prediction export and obtain an initial task score.

children.name: Test one controlled change
children.description: Hold the checkpoint, data, and other settings fixed while adding or reverting one factor to isolate its effect.

children.name: Measure repeated-run variation
children.description: Repeat a fixed configuration and compare score distributions before treating a small difference as an improvement.

children.name: Bracket a bounded search
children.description: Use a recorded coarse-to-fine or small factorial sweep over a specified parameter range, including nearby reversals.

children.name: Recover the last validated configuration
children.description: Restore the known-good configuration, or revert the suspected harmful factor, before resuming incremental experiments.

children.name: Stop an exhausted local search
children.description: Freeze the best validated setting after repeated changes fail to beat the noise floor and move the next experiment to a different lever.

children.name: Replace a clearly inadequate baseline
children.description: Test a coherent package of strongly motivated changes when establishing competitiveness matters more than attributing each component.

children.name: Repair prediction correctness
children.description: Choose a repair when predictions are missing, implausible, or inconsistent with the trained model.
children.decision: Where is there direct evidence that the prediction pipeline is wrong?

children.name: Repair artifact loading
children.description: Choose the correction required to load the intended trained computation.
children.decision: What prevents the intended checkpoint from being loaded correctly?

children.name: Verify artifact paths and lifetime
children.description: Resolve every configured checkpoint and prediction path, check existence, and defer cleanup until after its final use.

children.name: Resolve dependency and import conflicts
children.description: Use the required locally available package version and correct import path before constructing the model.

children.name: Match architecture to the checkpoint
children.description: Reconstruct the exact checkpoint architecture and tokenizer, normalize known wrapper prefixes, and require matching parameter keys and shapes.

children.name: Verify loaded weights are effective
children.description: Inspect loaded tensors and model mode, then run known examples to confirm trained weights actually drive non-degenerate outputs.

children.name: Repair data and output flow
children.description: Choose the stage whose observable invariant is broken.
children.decision: Which data-flow invariant is failing?

children.name: Trace rows and executed branches
children.description: Assert row IDs, shapes, columns, loop counts, and the final exported variable so every intended model contributes to the correct samples.

children.name: Audit intermediate feature tensors
children.description: Inspect representative tensors after each transformation and forward-pass operation to find wrong variables, axes, or disabled paths.

children.name: Restore training-time preprocessing
children.description: Apply the saved training encoders, feature extraction, resolution, and normalization in the same order at inference.

children.name: Reuse encoders with unknown-category handling
children.description: Transform test categories with the training-fitted encoder and an explicit policy for unseen values instead of refitting it.

children.name: Remove unavailable or leaking inputs
children.description: Remove identifier leakage and label-derived preprocessing dependencies, then rebuild transformations using only prediction-time information.

children.name: Compare outputs across a refactor
children.description: Run the saved and refactored pipelines on identical rows and compare aligned intermediate and final predictions numerically.

children.name: Repair prediction semantics
children.description: Choose the violated numerical contract before changing model quality.
children.decision: Which numerical mismatch explains the implausible predictions?

children.name: Align prediction units and direction
children.description: Convert logits or scaled targets correctly and align risk versus survival direction before scoring or blending.

children.name: Correct ensemble arithmetic
children.description: Convert predictions to numeric arrays and verify active-member divisors, group means, weights, and output scale.

children.name: Locate non-finite values
children.description: Check inputs and intermediate outputs for NaNs or infinities and repair the first stage that creates invalid values.

children.name: Correct the prediction or preprocessing API
children.description: Match method names, arguments, and mutation semantics to the actual model or dataframe object in use.

children.name: Restore a valid end-to-end run
children.description: Choose the smallest repair needed for a usable prediction artifact.
children.decision: What is preventing a valid full prediction run?

children.name: Debug a minimal end-to-end run
children.description: Run one model or a tiny data slice through all stages and fix the earliest failing operation before restoring scale.

children.name: Validate prediction export
children.description: Always write the final correctly aligned predictions to the required file with the expected schema, including in production mode.

children.name: Make missing-member handling explicit
children.description: Detect missing or corrupt member outputs and use only verified aligned fallback predictions or renormalized available members rather than placeholders.

children.name: Rebuild a tangled pipeline
children.description: Replace duplicated or fragile notebook paths with explicit reusable stages and validate equivalent behavior before adding further changes.

children.name: Remove execution bottlenecks
children.description: Choose an execution change that enables valid larger runs or more informative experiments.
children.decision: Which measured execution constraint is limiting useful experiments?

children.name: Reduce peak memory
children.description: Choose the object or operation whose memory footprint must shrink.
children.decision: What accounts for the memory peak?

children.name: Process data in bounded chunks
children.description: Partition examples by entity or split aggregations into smaller blocks, retaining only aligned predictions between blocks.

children.name: Release completed models and intermediates
children.description: Delete objects after their last use and clear runtime caches before loading the next model.

children.name: Reduce inference batch size
children.description: Find a batch size that completes inference and verify prediction invariance before using a larger batch for speed.

children.name: Compare reduced and full precision
children.description: Test reduced-precision inference against full precision on the same examples and retain it only when numerical effects are acceptable.

children.name: Shorten the iteration cycle
children.description: Choose which redundant work can be removed without changing the intended final computation.
children.decision: Which repeated work is slowing development?

children.name: Use a reduced development configuration
children.description: Gate reduced folds, seeds, rows, or iterations behind one explicit development setting and restore the full setting for final evaluation.

children.name: Cache stable intermediate artifacts
children.description: Save aligned embeddings, engineered features, predictions, or stage checkpoints once and reuse them while testing downstream changes.

children.name: Train unfinished folds across sessions
children.description: Persist each completed fold and resume only missing folds in later sessions.

children.name: Accelerate rank post-processing
children.description: Replace slow ranking code with a verified exact implementation, testing tied values and subgroup ordering before reusing it in adjustment searches.

children.name: Centralize variant configuration
children.description: Use named configurations and explicit artifact mappings to select models, feature branches, and blend members without scattered edits.

children.name: Change the runtime interface
children.description: Choose the interface change required by the observed execution limitation.
children.decision: Which runtime interface fits the required operation?

children.name: Use a supported execution backend
children.description: Move unsupported operations or model families to a verified CPU path, then enable acceleration only where the environment supports it.

children.name: Use the native training API
children.description: Move training to the native interface when custom callbacks or iteration control are unavailable in the current wrapper.

children.name: Use the estimator wrapper
children.description: Use the estimator interface when it provides the needed probability prediction and stopping behavior with less integration code.

children.name: Change the input information
children.description: Choose a representation change to expose missing signal or remove harmful inputs.
children.decision: What limitation in the current input representation should the next experiment address?

children.name: Change tabular summaries
children.description: Choose a reusable representation for repeated rows or interacting columns.
children.decision: Which information is missing from the current tabular summaries?

children.name: Inspect entity and feature structure
children.description: Profile record counts, time ordering, column families, dtypes, and missingness to determine the unit and scope of feature construction.

children.name: Use a minimal entity summary
children.description: Collapse repeated rows into a small last-value or basic-statistics baseline before expanding feature engineering.

children.name: Expand entity summary statistics
children.description: Add validated location, spread, range, count, or categorical-diversity aggregates to the entity-level features.

children.name: Summarize recent history separately
children.description: Add statistics over the most recent records alongside full-history entity aggregates and compare window lengths on held-out data.

children.name: Add change-over-time features
children.description: Compute ordered lag differences or first-to-last changes within entities and test their incremental value.

children.name: Add targeted interaction features
children.description: Construct a small set of domain-supported differences, ratios, or products, using smoothed summaries when individual values are noisy.

children.name: Encode elapsed or calendar time
children.description: Convert timestamps into elapsed-time or calendar features and test their value beyond existing entity summaries.

children.name: Reduce feature noise
children.description: Choose how to identify and remove inputs that do not generalize.
children.decision: What evidence should guide the next feature reduction?

children.name: Select a stable importance-ranked subset
children.description: Aggregate importance or attribution across folds and sweep the retention cutoff while checking held-out performance.

children.name: Ablate a suspected feature group
children.description: Remove or restore one coherent feature family and keep the smaller set only when validation supports it.

children.name: Test dropping extremely sparse columns
children.description: Remove columns above a measured missingness threshold and validate against retaining them.

children.name: Limit the pooled feature dimension
children.description: Compare the full pooled embedding with a truncated representation using a compatible trained head.

children.name: Change numerical preprocessing
children.description: Choose how to treat missingness and precision for the actual model family.
children.decision: Which numerical preprocessing policy fits the inputs and estimator?

children.name: Preserve native tree inputs
children.description: Trial removing unnecessary imputation, scaling, or outlier filtering when the tree implementation supports missing values directly.

children.name: Use model-specific imputation
children.description: Give models that require finite inputs a fitted imputation path while retaining native missingness where supported.

children.name: Coarsen noisy numerical precision
children.description: Round continuous inputs at a justified precision and compare against the original values on the same folds.

children.name: Change text information
children.description: Choose a text representation change based on what the pretrained encoder currently sees.
children.decision: What text information or formatting should be changed?

children.name: Change retained text context
children.description: Compare sequence length or task-relevant cropping only where truncation or irrelevant spans plausibly lose useful information.

children.name: Remove harmful custom cleaning
children.description: Compare aggressive cleaning with the pretrained tokenizer’s expected raw text and retain the better aligned input.

children.name: Change text-stream structure
children.description: Encode semantically distinct text fields separately or as a tested pair using checkpoints trained for that format.

children.name: Append structured text metadata
children.description: Concatenate validated text statistics or categorical metadata with the encoded text representation.

children.name: Change image or signal encoding
children.description: Choose the encoding parameter whose current setting plausibly hides relevant structure.
children.decision: Which aspect of the image or signal representation should be changed?

children.name: Sweep input spatial resolution
children.description: Compare nearby image resolutions with compatible checkpoints, holding other inference choices fixed.

children.name: Change the retained context window
children.description: Sweep temporal-window or spatial-crop extent around the current setting while preserving label alignment.

children.name: Change time-frequency resolution
children.description: Compare spectral transform, window, or hop settings with matched training preprocessing to trade temporal against frequency detail.

children.name: Match input normalization
children.description: Use validated per-sample or training-domain normalization consistently in training and inference.

children.name: Change signal filtering
children.description: Test a domain-supported notch, bandpass, or filter implementation while preserving a matched training/inference signal path.

children.name: Tune signal dynamic-range clipping
children.description: Compare nearby clipping thresholds for raw or log-spectral values to suppress extreme artifacts without removing informative signal.

children.name: Test scalar-to-color encoding
children.description: Compare colormap-based channels with the original scalar representation using a compatible pretrained image model.

children.name: Change signal-to-image layout
children.description: Compare height-width factorizations that preserve the sample values while changing the spatial neighborhoods seen by the image backbone.

children.name: Change modality use
children.description: Choose how to add, remove, or fuse complementary input streams.
children.decision: What should change in how input branches supply information?

children.name: Add derived input channels
children.description: Expose additional signal channels or derived features with matching model input dimensions and normalization.

children.name: Add a complementary model branch
children.description: Train or load a compatible branch for another modality or resolution and evaluate the resulting joint model.

children.name: Remove or restore an input branch
children.description: Ablate one modality at a time and retain it only if it improves the fixed model or ensemble comparison.

children.name: Compare concatenation with averaging
children.description: Test concatenated versus averaged branch embeddings with the corresponding trained head dimensions.

children.name: Change the training signal
children.description: Choose a data, target, or augmentation change rather than altering prediction combination.
children.decision: What limits the usefulness of the current labeled training signal?

children.name: Change training examples
children.description: Choose which examples should contribute to fitting the model.
children.decision: How should the training population change?

children.name: Refit on more labeled rows
children.description: After model selection, compare a smaller reserved holdout or a full-data refit using a separately established validation protocol.

children.name: Trial additional labeled data
children.description: Add compatible external labeled examples, optionally in an earlier training stage, and validate whether their distribution helps.

children.name: Train with validated pseudo-labels
children.description: Retrain a weak member with the available pseudo-labeling procedure and compare it with the labeled-only model.

children.name: Filter noisy or redundant examples
children.description: Compare quality thresholds, class filters, or deduplication using held-out evidence, retaining informative ambiguous examples when filtering harms performance.

children.name: Tune class or sample weights
children.description: Sweep moderate class-weight values against an unweighted baseline using the task metric rather than assuming full inverse-frequency balancing.

children.name: Change target construction
children.description: Choose how to express a censored or subgroup-dependent outcome for learning.
children.decision: Should target construction be global or conditioned on evaluation groups?

children.name: Transform the censored outcome
children.description: Compare regression-friendly survival or risk transforms and their scalar parameters while fitting target transformations within training folds.

children.name: Construct targets within evaluation groups
children.description: Estimate the outcome transformation separately for known evaluation groups and compare group and aggregate held-out performance.

children.name: Change training augmentation
children.description: Choose a training perturbation justified by the input and label structure.
children.decision: Which training augmentation is compatible with the task’s invariances?

children.name: Use mild image perturbations
children.description: Trial small brightness, contrast, or geometric changes and avoid magnitudes that distort domain-relevant image structure.

children.name: Mask local signal regions
children.description: Apply stochastic time-frequency masking during training and validate against the unmasked baseline.

children.name: Blend examples and soft labels
children.description: Compare multi-example mixup with the existing mixing scheme while preserving corresponding soft-label weights.

children.name: Change the model or fitting procedure
children.description: Choose a single-model intervention based on capacity, representation, or convergence evidence.
children.decision: Which single-model limitation should be addressed next?

children.name: Change the predictor family
children.description: Choose an alternative predictor according to the existing representation and checkpoint evidence.
children.decision: What kind of predictor change fits the current data and available artifacts?

children.name: Compare a different model family
children.description: Train or load a structurally different predictor on the same valid evaluation split and compare with the incumbent.

children.name: Change the pretrained backbone
children.description: Compare a compatible backbone or domain-pretrained checkpoint while holding downstream inference choices fixed.

children.name: Change backbone capacity
children.description: Compare smaller and larger trained backbone variants with matching head dimensions and preprocessing.

children.name: Fit a regressor on fixed embeddings
children.description: Extract aligned pretrained representations and fit a regularized classical or small neural predictor on held-out splits.

children.name: Add a retrieval predictor
children.description: Use training-only nearest neighbors in an embedding space as features or predictions and validate their incremental value.

children.name: Compare boosting variants
children.description: Test the alternative boosting strategy against the tuned incumbent using an appropriate iteration budget and stopping policy.

children.name: Change the prediction head
children.description: Choose a head change that matches the observed representation bottleneck.
children.decision: Which head modification should be compared with the current trained head?

children.name: Enrich the prediction head
children.description: Add a validated attention, normalization, or hidden-layer component between the backbone and prediction output, retraining a compatible checkpoint.

children.name: Simplify the prediction head
children.description: Compare a simpler shared or minimally normalized head with the current complex head using correctly matched trained weights.

children.name: Change representation pooling
children.description: Compare learned layer weighting or token mean/max/attention pooling using checkpoints trained for each pooling configuration.

children.name: Add an auxiliary prediction task
children.description: Train a parallel discretized classification or summary-target head alongside the main task and ablate its contribution.

children.name: Change tree fitting
children.description: Choose the tree-control adjustment indicated by fit and generalization evidence.
children.decision: What tree-fitting change should be tested next?

children.name: Sweep tree depth or leaf capacity
children.description: Compare bounded tree-depth or leaf-count settings on the fixed feature set, then recheck coupled regularization when needed.

children.name: Tune tree regularization
children.description: Sweep leaf-size constraints or coefficient penalties on a coarse scale, reverting uncertain overrides to validated defaults.

children.name: Introduce row and feature sampling
children.description: Test stochastic row and column subsampling against full-data tree construction with enough stopping patience.

children.name: Couple learning rate and boosting budget
children.description: Adjust learning rate together with sufficient boosting rounds and patience so comparisons do not confuse slow learning with undertraining.

children.name: Reduce per-member boosting duration
children.description: Compare shorter tree fits when ensemble averaging may permit lower individual complexity.

children.name: Change neural optimization
children.description: Choose an optimization adjustment based on observed training behavior.
children.decision: Which optimization control should be changed first?

children.name: Bracket the fine-tuning learning rate
children.description: Compare nearby learning rates with controlled training duration and retreat from rates that destabilize validation.

children.name: Compare learning-rate schedules
children.description: Test a different decay schedule while holding optimizer and other training settings fixed.

children.name: Compare optimizers
children.description: Evaluate an alternative optimizer against the current one on identical data and model configurations.

children.name: Tune head dropout
children.description: Sweep head dropout during training and recheck nearby learning rates using compatible trained checkpoints.

children.name: Align the loss and output parameterization
children.description: Compare a task-appropriate loss and activation, such as independent outputs or pairwise ranking, against the current objective.

children.name: Change training duration or checkpoint use
children.description: Choose how fitting should stop and which trained state should be retained.
children.decision: What limits the quality of the currently selected trained state?

children.name: Sweep training duration
children.description: Compare adjacent epoch or iteration budgets and keep the state that generalizes best under the validated evaluation protocol.

children.name: Retune early-stopping patience
children.description: Compare stopping patience around the current setting using the learning rate and validation-curve variability as context.

children.name: Compare existing trained checkpoints
children.description: Evaluate saved epochs, stages, or runs with fixed preprocessing and combination settings before selecting a checkpoint.

children.name: Average compatible model weights
children.description: Average compatible late-training weight states and validate against the original checkpoint before using the smoothed model.

children.name: Repair and retune a weak member’s training
children.description: Improve and validate an individual component’s representation or training discipline before building a blend around it or increasing its contribution.

children.name: Change prediction combination
children.description: Choose how to obtain complementary predictions and combine them using held-out evidence.
children.decision: Which limitation in the current ensemble should be addressed next?

children.name: Change the active member set
children.description: Choose an inclusion experiment rather than changing weights at the same time.
children.decision: What membership experiment is justified by the existing component evidence?

children.name: Trial one additional candidate
children.description: Add one validated prediction source to the fixed baseline blend and retain it only if its marginal contribution generalizes.

children.name: Replace one ensemble slot
children.description: Swap a single member or checkpoint group while freezing other members and the initial combination rule.

children.name: Ablate or prune active members
children.description: Remove one active prediction source at a time, recompute the valid blend, and retain removals supported by held-out results.

children.name: Compare a member with the ensemble
children.description: Score individual members and the fixed ensemble on the same rows to establish whether combining them adds value.

children.name: Restore a proven diverse blend
children.description: Re-enable the previously validated contributing members after pruning or an isolated probe degraded performance.

children.name: Choose a source of diversity
children.description: Choose how to generate a prediction source with a different error pattern.
children.decision: Which source of additional prediction diversity is available and underrepresented?

children.name: Add a different model family
children.description: Generate compatible predictions from an underrepresented architecture or algorithm and test its contribution to the existing ensemble.

children.name: Add a different input representation
children.description: Train or load a model using a distinct feature set, modality, resolution, or preprocessing path and test its ensemble contribution.

children.name: Add a different target encoding
children.description: Fit a model to an alternative valid target transformation and evaluate whether its aligned predictions complement existing members.

children.name: Average independent training runs
children.description: Generate predictions from multiple independent training seeds and increase the count only while held-out gains persist.

children.name: Average more fold checkpoints
children.description: Include additional compatible held-out-fold models and compare the larger average with the existing fold set.

children.name: Select a validated fold subset
children.description: Compare the full fold average with individually validated fold subsets, avoiding selection from tiny noisy score differences alone.

children.name: Change blend weights
children.description: Choose a weighting rule supported by the strength and reliability of the available evidence.
children.decision: How should the active prediction sources be weighted?

children.name: Use equal member weights
children.description: Use a simple equal-weight average as the validated baseline when quality differences or manual weight gains are unreliable.

children.name: Optimize fixed blend weights
children.description: Sweep fixed member weights on aligned held-out predictions, retuning after component changes and retaining only gains larger than evaluation noise.

children.name: Test signed blend coefficients
children.description: Compare allowing negative coefficients with a nonnegative blend under held-out evaluation.

children.name: Weight model groups separately
children.description: Average folds or related members within each group, then blend group outputs so group size does not dictate influence.

children.name: Replace unstable adaptive weights
children.description: Use fixed validated coefficients instead of weights estimated from a tiny or unstable inference batch.

children.name: Test class-specific blend weights
children.description: Compare per-class weights with the global blend when component quality differs consistently by class.

children.name: Change the combination domain
children.description: Choose what quantities to average without confusing rank information with calibrated probabilities.
children.decision: On what scale should member predictions be combined?

children.name: Preserve raw member magnitudes
children.description: Use raw-score averaging when validated magnitude information or downstream additive corrections would be lost by ranking.

children.name: Trial per-target rank averaging
children.description: Compare averaging member ranks with raw averaging on fixed members and recheck after changes to their output distributions.

children.name: Normalize prediction columns
children.description: Fit standard or robust scaling on out-of-fold member predictions and apply the same transformation before recomputing blend weights.

children.name: Trial a concave probability transform
children.description: Compare a power transform of each member’s probabilities before blending against the untransformed blend.

children.name: Average logits before softmax
children.description: Compare weighted logit averaging followed by softmax with the probability-average baseline.

children.name: Normalize each member before averaging
children.description: Apply the appropriate probability link to each member first and average the resulting distributions.

children.name: Change the stacking stage
children.description: Choose the appropriate level of learned combination for the available held-out data.
children.decision: What change to learned stacking is supported by the current evidence?

children.name: Compare learned stacking with averaging
children.description: Train a regularized stacker on aligned out-of-fold predictions and retain it only if it beats the validated fixed blend.

children.name: Compare meta-learner families
children.description: Test a low-capacity linear, kernel, or tree meta-learner on the same held-out meta-features and revert added complexity that does not generalize.

children.name: Tune meta-learner regularization
children.description: Search a bounded regularization and solver range for the existing meta-learner, comparing against a stable default.

children.name: Change the stacker’s feature set
children.description: Add or remove validated prediction, embedding, or auxiliary columns and retrain the stacker on the matching out-of-fold feature schema.

children.name: Change inference or output adjustment
children.description: Choose an inference-time action after verifying that the base predictions are correct.
children.decision: What residual prediction problem can be addressed without changing the base training data?

children.name: Change inference averaging
children.description: Choose whether variation across inference passes should be introduced or eliminated.
children.decision: Which inference-pass policy fits the task and current stochastic behavior?

children.name: Compare valid test-time views
children.description: Average predictions over justified flips, crops, channel symmetries, or resolutions and compare with a fixed single-view baseline for each model.

children.name: Trial stochastic dropout inference
children.description: Average genuinely stochastic dropout-enabled passes and compare against deterministic evaluation without assuming configuration dropout is active.

children.name: Make inference deterministic
children.description: Disable unintended stochastic transforms and dropout, pin random sources, and verify repeatable predictions before comparing models.

children.name: Change output calibration
children.description: Choose an adjustment justified by the meaning and observed bias of the predictions.
children.decision: What systematic output mismatch should be corrected?

children.name: Correct a validated prediction offset
children.description: Estimate a damped bias or reference-example correction from held-out evidence and compare it with the unshifted output.

children.name: Tune logit temperature before blending
children.description: Compare temperature-scaled component probabilities in the complete blend, distinguishing calibration effects from unchanged standalone ranks.

children.name: Reweight class probabilities
children.description: Test per-class probability multipliers followed by row normalization against the unadjusted categorical distribution.

children.name: Enforce the required output range
children.description: Apply only the required range or probability-simplex normalization, avoiding an extra softmax on already normalized probabilities.

children.name: Keep the raw ordered predictions
children.description: Remove unvalidated clipping or scaling when it adds no useful information to the metric or disrupts a downstream mapping.

children.name: Change output granularity
children.description: Choose how to handle discrete labels and ties without collapsing informative rankings.
children.decision: What should be done about discreteness or ties in the predictions?

children.name: Map predictions to label levels
children.description: Compare per-target thresholds or quantile mapping to observed label support with continuous predictions on held-out data.

children.name: Fall back for collapsed columns
children.description: Detect columns made constant by discretization and preserve their original continuous predictions.

children.name: Test tie handling explicitly
children.description: Compare deterministic tie preservation with a tightly bounded tie-breaking probe only when the metric’s tie treatment makes it justified.

children.name: Change structured output corrections
children.description: Choose a correction only when the auxiliary evidence exists at prediction time.
children.decision: Which structured correction, if any, has supporting evidence?

children.name: Use a validated auxiliary prediction
children.description: Test confidence-gated or additive adjustments from a compatible auxiliary classifier or second head on the final prediction scale.

children.name: Apply a high-precision metadata rule
children.description: Test a narrowly supported metadata-based adjustment for specific targets and reject broader heuristics that disrupt correct ordering.

children.name: Remove or restore an output correction
children.description: Ablate the existing post-processing while holding models fixed, restoring it only when its contribution remains validated.

unassigned.reason: Configures notebook progress-bar rendering and registration; it changes presentation rather than predictive performance or experimental validity.
